subject: Overage deferral & billing staircase for June burst
messages:
From: Elena Ruiz <elena@starlite.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.in>
Cc: Starlite Procurement <procurement@starlite.ai>
Date: Fri, 05 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Overage deferral options for June surge

Hi Karthik,

Quick note — we saw a 3x spike in inference tokens during our June marketing push and are already at 140% of our monthly quota. Procurement asked whether Redwood can provide a short-term option to avoid immediate overage charges while we sort internal approvals.

Specifically: would Redwood consider deferring overage invoicing for up to 90 days and allowing us a temporary headroom increase (up to 2x our committed quota) for the remainder of the month? If there are fees or a specific amortization schedule you require, please outline options so we can take this to our finance team.

We can share the June usage export (attached) and are open to a letter-of-credit or prepay if that simplifies approval.

Thanks — appreciate a quick path here.

Elena Ruiz
Head of Platform Ops | Starlite AI
elena@starlite.ai

Attachment: starlite-usage-june.csv (CSV, 42KB)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.in>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena@starlite.ai>
Cc: Starlite Procurement <procurement@starlite.ai>
Date: Fri, 05 Jun 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Overage deferral options for June surge

Hi Elena — thanks for the heads-up and the usage file. We can absolutely help avoid an immediate overage invoice while you finalize approvals.

High-level proposal ("billing staircase" approach):
- Temporary headroom: +2x committed quota through 30 Jun (no throttling).
- Deferral schedule: overage value accrued in June is invoiced on a staircase: 25% due at invoice issuance (within 7 days), 50% due at 30 days, final 25% due at 90 days.
- Surcharge: 8% one-time surcharge on the deferred overage balance to cover risk and cashflow (we're open to negotiating this down with collateral).
- Collateral options: letter-of-credit, 30% prepay, or joint escrow. If Starlite can provide LoC, we can waive 50% of the surcharge.
- Optional: if you convert a portion of this burst to a 3-month reserved increment (commit), we can apply a 10% credit against the surcharge.

I've attached a short term-sheet stub that lays this out. If this model works, we'll route a final term sheet + DocuSign to your procurement team and create a one-off invoice schedule in our billing system.

Next steps I suggest:
1) Tell me which collateral option Procurement prefers (LoC vs prepay).
2) Confirm whether you want the 3-month reserved conversion option evaluated.
3) If agreed, I'll loop Finance (Lauren) to lock the amortization and get final sign-off.

On point 3 — looping Lauren and Monica.

Thanks,

— Karthik Iyer
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference
karthik@redwood.in
Attachment: redwood-term-sheet-billing-staircase.pdf (PDF, 18KB)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.in>
To: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.in>, monica_patel <monica_patel@redwood.in>
Date: Fri, 05 Jun 2026 10:07:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Overage deferral options for June surge

Forwarding Starlite's ask — they want a 90-day deferral and a 2x temporary headroom. My proposed staircase is 25/50/25 with an 8% surcharge (waivable to 4% with LoC). Also offered a conversion credit if they commit to a 3-month reserved uplift.

Can finance sign off on the 25/50/25 amortization and the waiver mechanics with LoC? If you prefer, we can change the amortization to 30/40/30 or shorten to 60 days for the middle tranche.

Also flagging risk: customer has high burst variability; suggest we require usage caps in billing system and a short-term monitoring hook so we get notified if usage continues to accelerate.

Thanks — Karthik

From: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.in>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.in>, monica_patel <monica_patel@redwood.in>
Date: Fri, 05 Jun 2026 11:23:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Overage deferral options for June surge

Karthik — read and noted. A few comments from finance:

1) Amortization: 25/50/25 is acceptable from a cashflow perspective, but we'd prefer clearer milestones tied to invoice dates (Day 0, Day 30, Day 90) with automated reminders.
2) Surcharge: 8% is a bit high for a strategic customer. Recommend 6% standard, and drop to 3% with LoC. If they agree to convert >= 30% of the burst into a 3-month commit, drop base surcharge to 4% and waive entirely on the converted portion.
3) Collateral: LoC documents must be reviewed by Legal; procurement-provided LoCs typically add 3 business days. Prepay is fastest but requires procurement approval.
4) Accounting: need to tag the deferred overage as "one-off receivable" and ensure our billing system creates milestone invoices; I can provision the invoice schedule once procurement confirms the method.

If we go with these terms I'll sign-off; Monica — from CS, do you want a smaller commitment to keep them happy (3-month trial), or should we be firm?

Lauren Bishop
Director, Revenue Operations | Redwood Inference
lauren_bishop@redwood.in

From: monica_patel <monica_patel@redwood.in>
To: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.in>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.in>
Date: Fri, 05 Jun 2026 12:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Overage deferral options for June surge

Agree with Lauren. My read on Starlite: they want breathing room, but we're in a good spot to ask for a short commit in exchange. Proposal from CS:

- Offer: 2x temporary headroom (through end of month) + 90-day deferral on overage.
- Pricing: 6% surcharge on deferred balance; reduce to 3% with LoC.
- Conversion incentive: if they convert >= 30% of the burst to a 3-month reserved uplift, apply a 10% usage credit applied to their next bill (effectively lowers net surcharge).
- Operational guardrails: set a soft cap at 2.5x with auto-alerts and an emergency throttling policy if usage exceeds 3x.

I'll draft the short-term commitment language and the monitoring plan we can attach to the term sheet. If Procurement prefers prepay, we can shorten the deferral to 60 days and reduce surcharge to 4%.

Monica Patel
Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
monica_patel@redwood.in

From: Elena Ruiz <elena@starlite.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.in>
Cc: Starlite Procurement <procurement@starlite.ai>
Date: Mon, 08 Jun 2026 14:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Overage deferral & billing staircase for June burst

Thanks — this is helpful and aligns with what Procurement will accept in principle. Two quick asks before we sign:

1) Can you produce a finalized term sheet with the following variants so Procurement can review legal and treasury impact?
   a) 6% surcharge, LoC reduces to 3% (90-day staircase)
   b) 4% surcharge, 60-day staircase if Starlite prepays 30% of the deferred balance
   c) 0% surcharge on converted usage if we commit 30% to a 3-month reserved uplift

2) Please include explicit invoice milestones and language stating that the temporary headroom will be lifted automatically on 01 Jul unless converted.

If you can send the term sheets and DocuSign link today, Procurement will prioritize review. We'll provide the LoC template if we go that route. Also confirm whether this alters our SLA - we assume production SLAs remain unchanged during the headroom window.

We appreciate the flexible approach.

Best,
Elena
